mechanisms.causalChain: A policy/inflation/supply shock raises risk-free rates, term premia, FX basis or borrower-specific spreads; asset repricing and margin/collateral calls may constrain intermediaries; maturing liabilities then refinance at higher costs or fail to roll; weaker cash flow and investment can lower collateral and repayment capacity, creating lender losses and tighter credit. Central-bank facilities can bridge solvent institutions facing liquidity pressure, while fiscal restructuring, recapitalization or loss allocation is needed for insolvency.
mechanisms.counterEvidence: BIS measured cross-border bank credit was +11% y/y to USD 39.5tn at end-Q1 2026 and USD/EUR foreign-currency nonbank credit measures also grew. That rebuts contraction in those aggregates, not stress in marginal borrowers. High cash, fixed coupons, hedging, longer maturities, deposits, local markets and official backstops can dampen pass-through; the IMF April 2026 report described risks and amplification channels while noting markets had remained orderly to date.
mechanisms.stockFlowTransmission: Debt, liquid assets, collateral and capital are balance-sheet stocks; interest expense, new issuance, repayments, asset sales and credit growth are flows. For each borrower, track opening debt plus issuance minus principal repayment and write-offs, with FX/price valuation separated. Refinancing cost applies to new borrowing and maturing/reset debt, not instantly to every outstanding fixed-rate liability. Treat market depth/spreads separately from credit quantities.
mechanisms.identificationLimits: BIS GLI covers specified foreign-currency credit to nonbanks and BIS LBS locational banking positions; neither measures all global liquidity, domestic lending, shadow credit, market depth, borrower solvency or maturity. IMF GFSR risk mapping and financial-accelerator literature support channels but do not identify a 2026–30 aggregate causal multiplier. Common shocks, endogenous risk premia and policy response complicate identification.
mechanisms.modelability: Modelable as a segmented balance-sheet bridge with rate curves, borrower spreads, currency, maturity/reset schedules, hedges, cash, collateral haircuts and policy liquidity; aggregate credit growth is a descriptive check, not a calibration of defaults or output multipliers.
mechanisms.scenarioRelevance: Stress test sustained rates and spreads against actual refinancing needs and cash-flow buffers across regions; distinguish orderly repricing from funding-market discontinuity and solvency losses.
mechanisms.unresolvedUncertainty: Matched current debt-service, maturity, currency and nonbank leverage data are incomplete across US, China, EU and Switzerland. Q1 2026 BIS is the latest observation in the accepted cutoff bundle; Q2 is unavailable at cutoff. There is no defensible single observed global liquidity quantity or crisis threshold.
mechanisms.investigationNotes: Primary support combines the BIS July 31 2026 statistical release, IMF April 2026 GFSR risk-channel findings, the BIS reconstruction of pre-2008 non-US bank dollar funding gaps and Federal Reserve swap-line retrospective, plus financial accelerator theory. Counterevidence is explicit: BIS quantity growth and orderly market assessment do not show a current generalized collapse. Modeling should transmit policy/risk shocks only through documented maturity, currency, collateral and cash-flow exposure segments; keep liquidity assistance distinct from solvency. Do not convert correlation, a broad credit stock or a scenario stress into probability.

mechanisms.causalChain: A source-country rate/risk repricing can lead foreign investors or lenders to rebalance; portfolio, bank, FDI and trade-credit exposures can transmit through prices, rollover needs, FX demand and affiliate earnings. Currency depreciation can raise local-currency debt burdens for unhedged borrowers, while weaker collateral and cash flow can tighten credit. Local-currency funding, capital controls, reserves, hedges, domestic investors, trade substitution and policy support alter each regional link. The refreshed BIS CBS panel contains seven numeric 2026-Q1 gross international-claim observations reported by FR- and GB-nationality banking groups on DE, CH, US and FR residents; it returned no numeric rows for the selected US, CN or CH reporter series, or for selected CN counterpart-residence combinations. GB is not an EU reporter, and bank nationality is not country residence. The bounded 2024 UN Comtrade comparison provides four observed reporter-export flows (US↔China and EU27→US/China); Swiss-pair and US→EU requests returned no rows. A separate 2018 OECD input-output proxy records EU suppliers at 54% of Swiss imported intermediate inputs. These measures bound links only; none is a causal output multiplier.
mechanisms.counterEvidence: The latest BIS snapshot shows expanding cross-border bank credit, not generalized retreat. IMF April 2026 finds risk sensitivity varies by investor type and recipient vulnerabilities, and opportunities as well as risks accompany flows. US dollar, euro and CHF safe-asset/deep-market roles, China capital controls and largely domestic RMB funding, EU cross-border integration, and Switzerland’s external asset/liability structure mean the same shock does not transmit symmetrically. FDI is usually longer-horizon and less liquid than portfolio holdings, though it can still be delayed or revalued. Switzerland has diversified imports (OECD 2018 data: EU 54%, Asia 17%, North America 10%, rest of Europe 8%, other 11%); gross international claims do not net reciprocal positions, and observed cross-border bank credit expanded in Q1 2026. The available comparison is incomplete: UN Comtrade Switzerland-directed and US→EU queries returned count=0, not measured zero; no complete mirror or value-added series was assembled. EU-to-US and EU-to-China values are reported by EU27; the separate US-China mirror values differ substantially, as is expected for independently compiled export records.
mechanisms.stockFlowTransmission: BIS LBS and consolidated statistics are different exposure stocks (residence/intragroup versus nationality/ultimate-risk views); IMF IIP/CDIS/CPIS report positions. BOP records transactions/flows. Reconcile positions by opening stock + transactions + exchange/price valuation + other volume/reclassification changes = closing stock. OECD ICIO and BEA IO are annual production/trade flow structures, not financial exposures. Avoid summing positions and flows or double-counting cross-border intermediates and imported value added. Newly extracted BIS CBS claims are outstanding gross USD-equivalent stocks on an immediate-counterparty basis, while OECD Swiss input shares are 2018 production-input flow relationships. They cannot be added together or interpreted as net exposure; transactions, currency and valuation changes, maturity, hedges and domestic channels remain separate. Goods exports are annual nominal flows; BIS claims are quarterly gross consolidated stocks by bank nationality to counterparty residence; country IIP is a different residence-based position. They must not be summed or netted. FX valuation, service trade, firm ownership, maturities and hedging remain outside these measures.
mechanisms.identificationLimits: Common monetary/risk shocks, endogenous FX/asset prices and two-way trade create confounding; global-cycle and monetary-shock research motivates hypotheses but coefficients depend on identification, sample and specification. CPIS/CDIS are incomplete and counterpart data may use immediate investor rather than ultimate risk. OECD ICIO 2025 ends in 2022 and the direct data archive was not extracted because the publisher endpoint returned an HTML CDN challenge; it is not treated as a complete 2026 flow matrix. The fresh BIS query is a selected bank-nationality-to-counterparty-residence panel with only seven numeric FR/GB rows, non-returned/suppressed combinations, no selected numeric US/CN/CH reporters and no complete EU aggregate; USD-equivalent gross claims do not identify net exposure. UN Comtrade values are reporter-specific nominal merchandise exports; Swiss-directed queries and the selected US→EU query returned count=0. Eurostat Comext responses did not produce a persisted usable comparison value. No matched cross-region financial matrix with currency, maturity, sector and hedge detail or causal spillover coefficient has been assembled.
mechanisms.modelability: Low for calibrated spillover magnitudes; moderate only for scenario architecture. Model the four reported merchandise edges and the separate lagged Swiss-EU input-share proxy as observed exposure bounds. Use financial stocks only for the seven sourced BIS edges with nationality/residence attribution. Any broader elasticities, missing cells, service/value-added flows or pass-through parameters must remain explicit scenario assumptions or be estimated from independently identified evidence; do not derive coefficients from this partial panel.
mechanisms.scenarioRelevance: Needed to test whether a US AI investment correction, China domestic deleveraging or external-flow shock spills to European suppliers and Swiss exporters/financial links, and whether portfolio safe-haven demand offsets trade/earnings losses. Model gross flow, exchange-rate and supply-chain channels separately and permit net effects of either sign.
mechanisms.unresolvedUncertainty: Current ultimate-risk exposures, private-credit links, trade-credit/FDI transmission, company hedges and current sectoral trade data remain unknown. National-data vintages and regional definitions (EU versus euro area; Switzerland outside EU; China onshore/offshore) require reconciliation. Complete US/China/EU27/Swiss bilateral trade and matched bank exposures by residence/nationality, currency, maturity and sector remain unavailable. BIS reporter coverage and immediate-counterparty attribution are partial; Q2 2026 observations were unavailable at the evidence cutoff. The comparison is a bounded observation set, not a total regional network or spillover elasticity.
mechanisms.investigationNotes: Global synthesis reuses BIS/IMF definitions, monetary transmission literature and OECD input-output context. The mechanism is architectural and does not assign a loss to a region from any particular shock. The 2025 OECD ICIO 2022-endpoint archive download returned an HTML CDN challenge and was not parsed as data. Alternative official-source search materialized 12 UN Comtrade directed 2024 export responses (four observations; eight count=0), reviewed Eurostat Comext ext_lt_maineu (an invalid-dimension request HTTP 400; a later multi-select request HTTP 200 without selected partner rows; a previously successful US request was not persisted and is excluded), and checked Swiss customs aggregate trade coverage (no partner rows in canonical extract). Fresh BIS CBS API v2 request metadata and raw CSV are archived; the bounded 2026-Q1 query returned seven numeric FR/GB bank-nationality rows. Non-returned values are not zeros. Verizon FY2001 excerpts are parsed from archived SEC annual report text and source-located in verizon-source-excerpts.json. WorldCom total debt is 29.310 long-term excluding current plus 1.309 current = 30.619 USD bn. The FFR reuse record uses the 3.875% range midpoint, not the upper bound.

mechanisms.causalChain: Historical episodes supply conditional sequences: credit-intensive investment and collateral expansion can precede deeper recessions; after losses, leverage, fixed obligations and limited refinancing can propagate the shock. A telecom infrastructure analogue can motivate testing oversupply, utilization, pricing, debt and salvage; the 2008–09 dollar funding crisis illustrates currency/maturity mismatch; property-price deflation episodes show collateral and private debt can interact. Whether mechanisms transfer depends on balance sheets, institutions, product demand, technology reuse, policy response and timing.
mechanisms.counterEvidence: Historical analogues are heterogeneous and selected ex post. BIS finds weak broad-sample association of goods/services price deflation with output, with stronger property/asset price relationships; even credit booms do not uniformly end in crisis. GAO’s Global Crossing record concerns a failed carrier and a specific contracting dispute, while contemporary large technology firms have broader cash-generative businesses, different debt and asset reuse options. Central banks and regulators now have different tools and frameworks than earlier episodes. Restated WorldCom FY2001 shows cash USD 1.29bn, operating cash flow USD 2.845bn, PPE additions USD 6.465bn, and long-term debt excluding current maturities USD 29.310bn (current portion USD 1.309bn; total debt USD 30.619bn); the same filing records a USD 70.8bn reduction to equity from restatement adjustments. Level 3 reported USD 2.3bn 2001 capex, USD 2.1bn available funds including an undrawn facility, and estimated USD 13–14bn cumulative capital need to reach FCF breakeven. Verizon is included as a surviving integrated incumbent comparator, but its regulated/local access and wireless mix makes it structurally unlike a long-haul entrant. The Verizon 2001 SEC-filed annual report provides a surviving incumbent bridge: cash USD 0.979bn, OCF USD 19.773bn, cash capex USD 17.371bn, and balance-sheet debt USD 64.326bn (USD 18.669bn due within one year plus USD 45.657bn long term). Its OCF less cash capex was USD 2.402bn; debt structure and regulated/wireless incumbent mix differ from WorldCom.
mechanisms.stockFlowTransmission: Compare leverage/cash/collateral/maturity stocks and fixed operating or financing commitments against revenues, interest, investment, debt issuance/repayment and asset sale flows. Historical time-series evidence speaks to conditional average outcomes across samples, not a company’s current balance sheet. Separate nominal goods-price deflation from asset-price deflation and disaggregate private versus public debt and bank versus nonbank liabilities.
mechanisms.identificationLimits: Small numbers of crises, survivorship/selection, changing institutions, sample composition, structural breaks, measurement differences and omitted policies limit causal transport. Local-projection controls do not eliminate all endogeneity. A close narrative match does not provide a scenario probability, loss severity, duration, or parameter estimate. The GAO Global Crossing decision is not a sector census; comparisons need survivors and primary filings too. The added comparison is an adversarial case table, not a matched sample: WorldCom has major fraud, acquisition accounting and diversified legacy operations; Level 3 was a fiber entrant and itself later restructured; Verizon was an integrated incumbent. These firm differences prevent attributing outcomes to overbuild alone. No harmonized utilization denominator or comparable realized fiber salvage/recovery price was found in the inspected primary disclosures.
mechanisms.modelability: Use analogues as stress-path design and qualitative sign checks. Calibrate quantitative model parameters to current issuer/sector data or clearly labeled bounded assumptions; do not use historical case outcomes as direct multipliers or crisis odds.
mechanisms.scenarioRelevance: Adversarially test both downside and adaptation: overbuild/price war and refinancing stress against cash buffers, contractual flexibility, demand growth, utilization, technology obsolescence/reuse, refinancing access and policy. Test AI infrastructure separately from 2001 telecom network economics and from 2008 wholesale dollar markets.
mechanisms.unresolvedUncertainty: The counterfactual path for current AI demand, efficient utilization, salvage/redeployment value, capex cancellation, refinancing spread and household/firm balance sheets is unknown. Current issuer-specific exposures and comparable nonfailed firms are needed to assess analogy proximity. Historical source samples do not resolve this forecast uncertainty. A complete failed-versus-surviving entrant cohort with comparable utilization, debt/coupon ladders, cash flows and realized asset recoveries remains unavailable in this repair. Verizon filing identity was verified; a harmonized numeric survivor bridge and common network-utilization metric remain unextracted.
mechanisms.investigationNotes: The JST long-run panel reports average association between credit-intensive expansions and subsequent recession depth/recovery; BIS historical deflation work explicitly differentiates goods price from asset/property deflation and finds material heterogeneity. BIS 2008 work documents an actual cross-border USD funding mechanism. The GAO record is a limited telecom failure case. Use these as causal-chain probes and robustness scenarios, not inevitability narratives. Counterevidence and sample limits must travel with each model output. Primary filing extraction persisted in telecom-analogue-comparison.json. WorldCom figures use restated SEC Form 10-K statements and debt note (FY2001); Level 3 figures are management disclosures in its FY2001 SEC-filed annual report. Verizon FY2001 Form 10-K accession verified from SEC, but was not forced into a numeric comparison where definitions and selected extraction could not be confirmed. This avoids a false matched comparison. Verizon survivor extraction is now persisted with source-located figures in telecom-analogue-comparison.json. WorldCom debt is explicitly split in every statement: USD 29.310bn long-term excluding current plus USD 1.309bn current equals USD 30.619bn total.
